intro.v: The young people below all want to go on a city tour with their family while they’re away on holiday. On the opposite page there are descriptions of eight city tours. Decide which tour would be most suitable for the people below.

content.v: Tours

If you like shopping, our city market tour is for you! Pick up second-hand designer clothes at much-reduced prices. Later, we’ll stop at an outdoor café and try the city’s famous milk drink – perfect on a hot day. Sit in a beautiful tree-lined square and watch street theatre at the end of the day.

Jog with us from one tourist hotspot to another, following a route through the city centre. The ancient clock tower, beautiful palace and old town hall are all on our route. Our tour ends at the top of City Hill, in a park full of birds and wild rabbits, from where you can look down over all the city neighbourhoods.

Our bus will take you to our favourite shopping district away from the centre, where you’ll get some great discounts. The local art college there puts on a free fashion show most weekends, too. We also offer discounts for the design museum if you take our tour.

Our walking tour takes you to all the major sights, so you won’t miss anything! We’ll also walk along Main Street, looking in the stores of top fashion brands. We’ll finish our day with hot drinks and cake at the City Café, made popular by the musicians who often play there.

Why not join one of our city biking tours? We show you the modern side of the city and also go over the mountain to a beautiful village, where we’ll have a delicious picnic by the river. Bird song is the only sound you’ll hear!

On this tour for museum-lovers, there’s a choice of places to visit. The City Gallery is now showing a range of art created in this area. Or you might prefer the Natural History Museum, or even the Sports Museum. We use trams to get around and stop at the hundred-year-old market, with tasty snacks available in the many cafés.

If you like cities but also enjoy peace and quiet, come with us to the biggest park in the city. Our guides are all local people who will be happy to talk to you about their experiences in the city. There are coffee and food stalls, and there’s a historic outdoor theatre, with free performances daily.

The best way to see a new city is on foot. If you agree, join us on a personalised tour. Choose from a selection of interesting activities, from photographing and studying the animals and birds that have made their homes here to attending a free daily concert in a historic building.

content.v: Young people’s cooking school
by Tom Alvarez, aged 13

When I was three, my mum and I started making biscuits together. We used cookie cutters shaped like cartoon monsters, which I loved. It was always like a game and never too challenging. I’m so grateful to my mum for introducing me to cooking that way. I think that’s the main reason why I love it so much now.

I sometimes watch TV programmes about cooking, but they’re about so many different kinds of things that it can be really hard to choose which one to watch. I sometimes wonder where the chefs find their unusual ingredients, and a lot of the time their methods are so difficult that I lose interest. There are some programmes about making dishes that are good for you, but I’m not sure how many teenagers actually watch those.

Because I’m so keen on cooking, last month my parents paid for me to go on a one-day cookery course, especially designed for 10–14-year-olds, at a famous restaurant. We all went to the restaurant kitchen and our teacher, Maurice, gave us white aprons and hats: it was just like being a proper chef! The others were all younger than me – I hoped they wouldn’t expect me to be the best. Before we started, we had juice and snacks while we decided what we wanted to make: desserts or pasta dishes. I chose a pasta dish.

After that, we didn’t sit down again for two hours – there was loads to do. We watched Maurice carefully show us exactly what we had to do at each stage, then we had a go ourselves. One boy dropped his ingredients all over the floor, but Maurice just smiled and showed us how to arrange our plates, pans and stuff to make the best use of our space – that’s advice I’ll never forget. I left my pasta to boil for five extra minutes, and I didn’t put quite enough salt in the sauce, but it was still pretty good. When we’d finished, we all sat down in the main restaurant and enjoyed tasting what everyone had produced. If I ever get to do another course there, I think I’ll pick desserts, because those were amazing.

content.v: The kakapo: saving an unusual bird

The kakapo, a type of parrot, is a New Zealand bird. Kakapos are unusual for two reasons. Firstly, they weigh a lot – up to 5 kg in some cases. Secondly, although they were once found in large numbers throughout the country, they have come close to disappearing, partly because they have, over time, lost the ability to fly.
But that is not the only reason. Another issue is that kakapos typically only produce babies when a particular tree, the rimu tree, has a large amount of fruit available for them to eat.
As a result, there are sometimes long periods of time during which no new babies are born, which affects overall numbers.

One year, when researchers were doing a project on the birds, they were only able to find 51 of them. The New Zealand government realised that something needed to be done, so they decided to change the birds’ location.

None of the animals that typically hunt them lived there. When the kakapos arrived, they were fitted with special devices which have allowed researchers to study the birds ever since, and see where they are on the islands.
The technology gives the birds access to food, by electronically opening or closing food boxes.

When a female kakapo produces a lot of eggs, researchers sometimes remove some. This is done when, for example, the mother bird would find it hard to feed a larger number of babies. The eggs are kept in a warm room until the young kakapos are born. The birds are then cared for by the researchers for four months, at which point they are put back out on the island.
Then, of course, there would be a negative effect on future numbers. Fortunately, the project seems to be working, as the population of kakapos is increasing.
Instead, the researchers watched the young birds carefully with cameras.
The kakapos were moved to three small islands.
The birds enjoy a wide range of different foods.
If they were any older, the birds might not be accepted by other kakapos.
After all, this makes them easy for other animals to catch.
The number of birds has risen in the past few years, however.
This generally happens only every two to four years.
The birds’ diet can even be controlled using the same equipment.
